record.paper_title: SYMMETRY AND COLORINGS: SOME RESULTS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
record.original_question: For every finite group G of odd order and every integer r > 1, must ms(G, r) be strictly larger than 1/r², where ms(G, r) is the normalized largest guaranteed size of a monochromatic symmetric subset in every r-coloring of G?

evidence.quote: For a group G and a number r define M S(G, r) to be the least upper bound of cardinal numbers τ such that for every r-coloring of the group G there exists a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G of size |A| ≥ τ . For finite groups G it is more preferable to work with the normed value ms(G, r) = M S(G,r) / |G| .
4.3. Question. Is ms(G, r) > 1 / r2 for every group G of odd order and every r > 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite group with identity e. A subset A ⊆ G is called symmetric if there exists g ∈ G such that A = gA^{-1}g, equivalently A is invariant under the involution x ↦ gx^{-1}g for some g ∈ G. For a positive integer r, an r-coloring of G is a map χ: G → {1, …, r}. Define
   MS(G, r) = sup { τ ≥ 0 : for every r-coloring χ of G there exists a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊆ G with |A| ≥ τ },
and the normalized quantity
   ms(G, r) = MS(G, r) / |G|.

Question: Is it true that for every finite group G of odd order and every integer r > 1,
   ms(G, r) > 1 / r² ?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related work on monochromatic symmetric subsets in colored groups (Banakh–Verbitsky–Vorobets, Protasov, and follow-up papers on finite abelian groups and Lobachevsky plane), but no source explicitly resolving the strict inequality ms(G,r) > 1/r² for all finite groups of odd order and all r > 1 was found. The status of this specific question could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry — Banakh, Verbitsky, Vorobets
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational work defining MS(G,r) and ms(G,r) and proving lower bounds for various groups.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework for ms(G,r) but does not settle the odd-order question with bound 1/r².

status_evidence.title: Monochrome symmetric subsets of colored groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies monochrome symmetric subsets in r-colorings of groups.
status_evidence.claim: Related results, no explicit resolution of the stated inequality found.

status_evidence.title: Monochrome Symmetric Subsets in Colorings of Finite Abelian Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds for ms(G,r) for finite abelian groups.
status_evidence.claim: Treats abelian case; does not resolve the general odd-order question.
